Document: Practice Direction – Civil Recovery Proceedings
Part 2 of 3
==================================================
## 7A.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.3] A statement of assets is a witness statement which sets out all the property which the maker of the statement owns, holds or controls, or in which he has an interest, giving the value, location and details of all such property. Information given in a statement of assets under this practice direction will be used only for the purpose of the civil recovery proceedings. ## 7A.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.4] The court –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.4] (1) will not make an exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet his reasonable legal costs (including an initial exclusion under paragraph 5B.1); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.4] (2) may set aside any exclusion which it has made for that purpose or reduce any amount specified in such an exclusion,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.4] if it is satisfied that the person has property to which the property freezing order or interim receiving order does not apply from which he may meet those costs. ## 7A.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.5] The court will normally refer to a costs judge any question relating to the amount which an exclusion should allow for reasonable legal costs in respect of proceedings or a stage in proceedings. ## 7A.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.6] Attention is drawn to section 245C of the Act and article 149 of the Order in Council (in relation to exclusions from property freezing orders) and to section 252 of the Act and article 157 of the Order in Council (in relation to exclusions from interim receiving orders). An exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet his reasonable legal costs must be made subject to the ‘required conditions’ specified in Part 2 of the Regulations. ## 7A.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.7] An exclusion made for the purpose of enabling a person to meet his reasonable legal costs will specify –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.7] (1) the stage or stages in civil recovery proceedings to which it relates;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.7] (2) the maximum amount which may be released in respect of legal costs for each specified stage; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.7] (3) the total amount which may be released in respect of legal costs pursuant to the exclusion. ## 7A.8

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.8] A person who becomes aware that his legal costs –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.8] (1) in relation to any stage in civil recovery proceedings have exceeded or will exceed the maximum amount specified in the exclusion for that stage; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.8] (2) in relation to all the stages to which the exclusion relates have exceeded or will exceed the total amount that may be released pursuant to the exclusion,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.8] should apply for a further exclusion or a variation of the existing exclusion as soon as reasonably practicable. ## Assessment of costs where recovery order is made

## 7B.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.1] Where the court –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.1] (1) makes a recovery order in respect of property which was the subject of a property freezing order, a prohibition order or an interim receiving order; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.1] (2) had made an exclusion from the property freezing order, prohibition order or interim receiving order for the purpose of enabling a person to meet his reasonable legal costs,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.1] the recovery order will make provision under section 266(8A) of the Act or article 177(10) of the Order in Council (as appropriate) for the payment of those costs. ## 7B.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.2] Where the court makes a recovery order which provides for the payment of a person’s reasonable legal costs in respect of civil recovery proceedings, it will at the same time order the detailed assessment of those costs. Parts 4 and 5 of the Regulations CPR, Part 47 as modified by Parts 4 and 5 of the Regulations and paragraphs 7B.3 to 7B.7 of this Practice Direction (“the civil recovery costs provisions”) apply to a detailed assessment pursuant to such an order. ## 7B.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.3] In detailed assessment proceedings to which the civil recovery costs provisions apply-

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.3] (1)    the paying party is the trustee for civil recovery;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.3] (2)    the receiving party is the person whose reasonable legal costs are payable pursuant to provision made in the recovery order under section 266(8A) of the Act or article 177(10) of the Order in Council; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.3] (3)    the relevant persons for the purpose of rule 47.6(2) includes the enforcement authority or the appropriate officer in addition to the persons referred to in paragraph 5.5 of Practice Direction 47 – Procedure for Detailed Assessment of Costs and Default Provisions. ## 7B.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.4] On commencing detailed assessment proceedings, the receiving party must, in addition to serving the documents listed in paragraph 5.2 of Practice Direction 47 on the paying party and all other relevant persons, serve a statement giving the date, amount and source of all interim payments which have been released in respect of any of those costs under Part 3 of the Regulations. ## 7B.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.5] By virtue of regulation 13(2) of the Regulations, detailed assessment proceedings must be commenced not later than 2 months after the date of the recovery order, and a request for a detailed assessment hearing must be filed not later than 2 months after the expiry of the period for commencing the detailed assessment proceedings. ## 7B.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.6] The documents which must accompany the request for a detailed assessment hearing must include copies of all exclusions from property freezing orders or interim freezing orders made by the court for the purpose of enabling the receiving party to meet the costs which are to be assessed, and of every estimate of costs filed in relation to such an exclusion. ## 7B.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7B.7] The receiving party’s costs will be assessed on the standard basis, subject to Part 5 of the Regulations (and in particular regulation 17, which specifies the hourly rates which may be allowed). Attention is also drawn to regulation 14, which provides that the amounts of any interim payments released in respect of the receiving party’s costs will be deducted from the costs allowed in accordance with Part 5 of the Regulations. ## Registers

## 7C

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7C] There will be kept in the Central Office of the Senior Courts at the Royal Courts of Justice, under the direction of the Senior Master, a register of external orders which the High Court has ordered to be registered. ## SECTION IIA – APPLICATIONS UNDER PART 4A OF THE ORDER IN COUNCIL IN RESPECT OF PROHIBITION ORDERS

## Applications

## 7D.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.1] An application for a prohibition order must be made—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.1] (1) to a High Court judge; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.1] (2) in accordance with CPR Part 23. ## 7D.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.2] CPR rule 23.10(2), Sections I to V of CPR Part 25 do not apply to applications for property freezing orders, interim receiving orders and management receiving orders. ## 7D.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.3] The application may be made without notice in the circumstances set out article 141E(1) of the Order in Council (in the case of an application for a prohibition order). ## 7D.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.4] An application for a prohibition order must be supported by written evidence which must confirm that—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.4] (1) it is relevant property identified in an external request, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.4] (2) proceedings have not been taken in relation to the property under Chapter 2 of Part 5 of the Order in Council. ## 7D.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.5] CPR Part 69 (court’s power to appoint a receiver) and Practice Direction 69 apply to an application for a management receiving order with the following modifications—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.5] (1) paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 69 does not apply; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7D.5] (2) the enforcement authority’s written evidence must always identify a nominee and include the information in paragraph 4.2 of that Practice Direction. ## Exclusions when making prohibition order

## 7E.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.1] When the court makes a prohibition order on an application without notice, it will normally make an initial exclusion from the order for the purpose of enabling the respondent to meet their reasonable legal costs so that they may—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.1] (1) take advice in relation to the order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.1] (2) prepare a statement of assets in accordance with paragraph 7A.3; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.1] (3) if so advised, apply for the order to be varied or set aside. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.1] The total amount specified in the initial exclusion will not normally exceed £3,000. ## 7E.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.2] When it makes a prohibition order, the court may also make an exclusion to enable the respondent to meet their reasonable legal costs so that (for example) when the claim is commenced—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.2] (1) the respondent may file an acknowledgment of service and any written evidence on which they intend to rely; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.2] (2) the respondent may apply for a further exclusion for the purpose of enabling them to meet their reasonable costs of the proceedings. ## 7E.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7E.3] Paragraph 7H contains general provisions about exclusions made for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs. ## Receiving order: application for directions

## 7F.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7F.1] An application for directions as to the exercise of the functions of the management receiver under article 141K of the Order in Council may be made at any time by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7F.1] (1) the receiver;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7F.1] (2) any party to the proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7F.1] (3) any person affected by any action taken, or proposed to be taken, by the receiver. ## 7F.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7F.2] The application must always be made by application notice, which must be served on—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7F.2] (1) the receiver (unless the receiver is the applicant);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7F.2] (2) every party to the proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7F.2] (3) any other person who may be interested in the application. ## Application to vary or set aside an order

## 7G.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.1] An application to vary or set aside a prohibition order (including an application for, or relating to, an exclusion from the order) may be made at any time by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.1] (1) the enforcement authority; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.1] (2) any person affected by the order. ## 7G.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.2] Unless the court otherwise directs or exceptional circumstances apply, a copy of the application notice must be served on—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.2] (1) every party to the proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.2] (2) any other person who may be affected by the court’s decision. ## 7G.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.3] Before exercising the power to discharge or vary a prohibition order, the court must give an opportunity for the parties, and any other person who may be affected by the court’s decision, to be heard, in accordance with article 141E of the Order in Council. ## 7G.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.4] The evidence in support of an application for an exclusion from a prohibition order for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.4] (1) contain full details of the stage or stages in proceedings under Part 4A of the Order in Council in respect of which the costs in question have been or will be incurred;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.4] (2) include an estimate of the costs which the person has incurred and will incur in relation to each stage to which the application relates;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.4] (3) include a statement of assets containing the information set out in paragraph 7A.3 (unless the person has previously filed such a statement in the same proceedings and there has been no material change in the facts set out in that statement);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.4] (4) where the court has previously made an exclusion in respect of any stage to which the application relates, explain why the person’s costs will exceed the amount specified in the exclusion for that stage; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.4] (5) state whether the terms of the exclusion have been agreed with the enforcement authority. ## 7G.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.5] Where, under paragraph 7G.4(2), a person includes in evidence a statement of the costs which the person has incurred, paragraphs 9.5(2) and (3) of Practice Direction 44 apply. ## 7G.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7G.6] A Master or District Judge may, with the consent of all the parties, vary or discharge a prohibition order granted by any judge. ## Exclusions for the purpose of meeting legal costs: general provisions

## 7H.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.1] Subject to paragraph 7H.2, when the court makes a prohibition order it will at the same time consider whether it is appropriate to make or vary an exclusion for the purpose of enabling any person affected by the order or directions to meet their reasonable legal costs. ## 7H.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.2] To enable the court to consider whether it is appropriate to make or vary an exclusion, the court may order a party to file an estimate of costs (unless the person has previously filed such an estimate in the same proceedings and there has been no material change in the facts set out in that estimate). ## 7H.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.3] The court will not make an exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs, other than an exclusion to meet the costs of taking any of the steps referred to in paragraph 7E.1, unless that person has made, served and filed a statement of assets. ## 7H.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.4] A statement of assets is a witness statement which sets out all the property which the maker of the statement owns, holds or controls, or in which  the maker of the statement has an interest, giving the value, location and details of all such property. Information given in a statement of assets under this practice direction will be used only for the purpose of the prohibition order proceedings, or in support of an application for an exclusion from a property freezing order or interim receiving order for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs (see paragraph 7.3). ## 7H.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.5] The court—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.5] (1) will not make an exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs (including an initial exclusion under paragraph 7E.1); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.5] (2) may set aside any exclusion which it has made for that purpose or reduce any amount specified in such an exclusion, if it is satisfied that the person has property to which the prohibition order does not apply from which the person may meet those costs. ## 7H.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.6] The court will normally refer to a costs judge any question relating to the amount which an exclusion should allow for reasonable legal costs in respect of proceedings or a stage in proceedings. ## 7H.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.7] Attention is drawn to article 141G of the Order in Council (in relation to exclusions from prohibition orders). An exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs must be made subject to the ‘required conditions’ specified in Part 2 of the Regulations. ## 7H.8

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.8] An exclusion made for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs will specify the maximum amount which may be released in respect of legal costs. ## 7H.9

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7H.9] A person who becomes aware that their legal costs will exceed the maximum amount specified should apply for a further exclusion or a variation of the existing exclusion as soon as reasonably practicable.”. ## How to apply for an order or warrant

## 8.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 8.1] An application for an order or warrant under Part 8 of the Act in connection with a civil recovery investigation or (where applicable), for an unexplained wealth order and an interim freezing order, or for an order or warrant under Part 1 of the 2013 Order in connection with an external investigation must be made –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 8.1] (1) to a High Court judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 8.1] (2) by filing an application notice. ## 8.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 8.2] The application may be made without notice, subject to section 362J(5) of the Act (where applicable). ## 8.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 8.3] CPR rule 23.10(2), Sections I to V of CPR Part 25 do not apply to applications for interim freezing orders. ## Confidentiality of court documents

## 9.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 9.1] CPR rules 5.4, 5.4B and 5.4C do not apply to an application under Part 8 of the Act (including an application for an unexplained wealth order or an interim freezing order) or an application under Part 1 of the 2013 Order, and paragraphs 9.2 and 9.3 below have effect in its place. ## 9.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 9.2] When an application is issued, the court file will be marked ‘Not for disclosure’ and, unless a High Court judge grants permission, the court records relating to the application (including the application notice, documents filed in support, and any order or warrant that is made) will not be made available by the court for any person to inspect or copy, either before or after the hearing of the application. ## 9.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 9.3] An application for permission under paragraph 9.2 must be made on notice to the appropriate officer, or (in the case of an application for an unexplained wealth order or an interim freezing order) the enforcement authority, in accordance with CPR Part 23. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 9.3] (CPR rule 23.7(1) requires a copy of the application notice to be served as soon as practicable after it is filed, and in any event at least 3 days before the court is to deal with the application.)

## Application notice and evidence

## 10.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 10.1] The application must be supported by written evidence, which must be filed with the application notice. ## 10.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 10.2] The evidence must set out all the matters on which the appropriate officer, or (in the case of an application for an unexplained wealth order or an interim freezing order) the enforcement authority, relies in support of the application, including any matters required to be stated by the relevant sections of the Act or (where applicable) the relevant articles of the 2013 Order, and all material facts of which the court should be made aware. ## 10.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 10.3] There must also be filed with the application notice a draft of the order sought. This should if possible also be supplied to the court in an electronic version in a form compatible with the word processing software used by the court. ## Hearing of the application

## 11.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 11.1] The application will be heard and determined in private, unless the judge hearing it directs otherwise. ## Variation or discharge of order or warrant

## 12.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1] An application to vary or discharge an order or warrant under Part 8 of the Act in connection with a civil recovery investigation, or for an order or warrant under Part 1 of the 2013 Order in connection with an external investigation, may be made by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1] (1) the appropriate officer or, in the case of a disclosure order, the relevant authority; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1] (2) any person affected by the order or warrant. ## 12.1A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1A] An application to vary or discharge an unexplained wealth order or an interim freezing order (including an application for, or relating to, an exclusion from the interim freezing order) may be made by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1A] (1) the enforcement authority; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1A] (2) any person affected by the order. ## 12.1B

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1B] Unless the Court otherwise directs or exceptional circumstances apply, a copy of the application notice must be served on—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1B] (1) every party to the proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1B] (2) any other person who may be affected by the court’s decision. ## 12.1C

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1C] The evidence in support of an application for an exclusion from an interim freezing order for the purpose of enabling a person to meet their reasonable legal costs must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1C] (1) contain full details of the stage or stages of proceedings under Chapter 2 of Part 8 of the Act in respect of which the costs in question have been or will be incurred;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1C] (2) include an estimate of the costs which the person has incurred and will incur in relation to each stage to which the application relates;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1C] (3) include a statement of assets containing the information set out in paragraph 7A.3 (unless the person has previously filed such a statement in the same proceedings and there has been no material change in the facts set out in that statement);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1C] (4) where the court has previously made an exclusion in respect of any stage to which the application relates, explain why the person’s costs will exceed the amount specified in the exclusion for that stage and state whether the terms of the exclusion have been agreed with the enforcement authority. ## 12.1D

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1D] Where, under paragraph 12.1C(2), a person includes in evidence a statement of the costs which the person has incurred, paragraphs 9.5(2) and (3) of Practice Direction 44 apply. ## 12.1E

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1E] Before exercising the power to discharge or vary an interim freezing order, the court must give an opportunity for the parties, and any other person who may be affected by the court’s decision, to be heard, in accordance with section 362K(9) of the Act. ## 12.1F

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1F] The court must discharge an interim freezing order in the circumstances set out in section 362K of the Act. ## 12.1G

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.1G] A Master or District Judge may, with the consent of all the parties, vary or discharge an interim freezing order granted by any judge. ## 12.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.2] An application under paragraph 12.1 or 12.1A to stop an order or warrant from being executed must be made immediately upon it being served. ## 12.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.3] A person applying to vary or discharge a warrant must first inform the appropriate officer that he is making the application. ## 12.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.4] The application should be made to the judge who made the order or issued the warrant or, if he is not available, to another High Court judge. ## Management receiving order in connection with an interim freezing order: application for directions

## 12.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.5] CPR Part 69 (court’s power to appoint a receiver) and Practice Direction 69 apply to an application for a management receiving order with the following modifications—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.5] (1) paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 69 does not apply; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.5] (2) the enforcement authority’s written evidence must always identify a nominee and include the information in paragraph 4.2 of that Practice Direction. ## 12.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.6] Where an application is made for a management receiving order, a draft of the order which is sought must be filed with the application notice. This should if possible also be supplied to the court in an electronic form compatible with the word processing software used by the court. ## 12.7

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.7] An application for directions as to the exercise of the functions of the management receiver under section 362P of the Act may be made at any time by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.7] (1) the management receiver;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.7] (2) any party to the proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.7] (3) any person affected by any action taken, or proposed to be taken, by the management receiver. ## 12.8

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.8] An application mentioned in paragraph 12.7 must always be made by application notice, which must be served on—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.8] (1) the management receiver (unless the management receiver is the applicant);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.8] (2) every party to the proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.8] (3) any other person who may be interested in the application. ## 12.9

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.9] An application to vary or set aside a management receiving order under section 362P of the Act (including an application for, or relating to, an exclusion from the order) may be made at any time by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.9] (1) the enforcement authority; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.9] (2) any person affected by the order. ## 12.10

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.10] Unless the court otherwise directs or exceptional circumstances apply, a copy of the application notice for an application mentioned in paragraph 12.9 must be served on–-

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.10] (1) every party to the proceedings;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.10] (2) the management receiver; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 12.10] (3) any other person who may be affected by the court’s decision. ## Production order

## 13.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.1] The application notice must name as a respondent the person believed to be in possession or control of the material in relation to which a production order is sought. ## 13.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.2] The application notice must specify –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.2] (1) whether the application is for an order under paragraph (a) or (b) of section 345(4) of the Act or, if the application is made under Part 1 of the 2013 Order, whether the application is for an order under paragraph (a) or (b) of article 6(4) of the 2013 Order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.2] (2) the material, or description of material, in relation to which the order is sought; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 13.2] (3) the person who is believed to be in possession or control of the material.
